function: Over-the-air aggregation of FL gradients: SCA-optimized ASTARS phase shifts and BS receive beamformer minimize aggregation error and improve FL test accuracy (p. 1, 6-7).
system: Uplink OTA-FL: BS with 5 antennas, 80 single-antenna users, active STARS (simultaneously transmitting and reflecting) with Q=30 elements, Rician fading, frequency not stated (p. 3, 8).
method: Federated learning of a CNN (MNIST) with over-the-air gradient aggregation; ASTARS phases and receive beamformer set by non-learned SCA optimization, batch and mini-batch gradient descent (p. 7, 9).
data_channel: Synthetic Rician channels BS-ASTARS and ASTARS-users with path loss (exponent 2); MNIST digits partitioned over devices as FL data (p. 3, 8, 9).
test_conditions: MNIST FL trained and tested under one simulated channel model; set 1 equal and set 2 unequal local data sizes; Q and amplification factor varied (p. 8-11).
baselines: Noise-free FL, PSTARS-FL, RIS-FL and FL without RIS, adjusted with the paper's SCA; ASTARS with MM and DC optimization; no earlier published OTA-FL design (p. 9-10).
metrics: FL test accuracy versus training round, number of ASTARS elements Q and amplification factor; analytic bound on aggregation error and learning loss (p. 6, 9-11).
complexity: SCA algorithm: O(Imax |Phi|^3) computational complexity (interior-point method per iteration) and O(Q^3) space complexity; no runtime reported (p. 8).
openness: None; no code or data link is given (MNIST used, p. 9).
q1_support: p. 3: "ASTARS uplink communication links experience Rician fading" - custom Rician channel with path loss exponent 2 and eta0 = -30 dB (Table II, p. 8); no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "In Fig. 4 and 5, we plot the test accuracy achieved with" different numbers of elements under set 1 and set 2 - each setting is a separate FL training run; no model is tested on a condition unseen in training and no adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 9: "All baselines are adjusted using" the proposed SCA algorithm (PSTARS-FL, RIS-FL and FL without RIS are the paper's own variants; MM and DC are generic optimizers); no earlier published OTA-FL aggregation design is simulated (Table I, p. 3, is a feature comparison only).
q4_support: p. 8: "overall computational complexity of Algorithm 1 is upper" bounded by O(Imax Phi^3), with O(Q^3) space complexity - the cost of the RIS phase-shift and beamformer design.
q5_support: p. 9: "we conduct experiments using the MNIST" dataset - a learning-task dataset only; the channel is simulated with a custom model (Table II, p. 8) and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included under the OTA-FL rule: the ASTARS phases and receive beamformer come from non-learned SCA optimization (p. 7), and the learned element is the FL model (CNN on MNIST) trained across devices (p. 9). Area 7 wins over area 3 because the problem is the OTA aggregation error. q3 is 0: the RIS and no-RIS baselines are the paper's own variants run with its SCA and MM/DC are generic optimizers; reviewer to confirm. The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint; it prints no DOI, so the match with the DOI could not be checked from the text.
